# `intent at`

**Generated by `intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/gen_reference.sh` at 2026-09-11 20:23Z. Do not edit -- re-run it.**

Acceptance tests: the small red-to-green tests that prove ACs

|                                      |                                                          |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Revision this describes              | `1c55a34853449be626399b513d4674080d5e0e52` (`1c55a3485`) |
| Release presence is reported against | `v3.0.1`                                                 |

**The register is a declaration, not a behaviour claim.** The command surface is built from `surface/dispatch-table.json`, so the register at a revision states what that revision exposes. It does not state that any of it works. Where this page and your binary disagree, **your binary is right**.

**No exit codes are listed per command.** The register's per-command exit tables are measurements of _v2_, and v3 does not reproduce them everywhere, so they are not published here as v3's contract. Every command follows the one surface-wide contract on the [index](index.md#exit-codes).

**Descriptions on this page that assert a precondition are flagged inline below.** Refusals have no declared home in the register, so they can only be stated as prose in a help string. The detector that finds them is a regex over English and is therefore a floor, not a ceiling: a precondition phrased without one of its words is invisible to it. Issue `0142`.

## The commands

| Command           | What it does                                                                      | In v3.0.1 | Reads or writes | Undo       |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | --------------- | ---------- |
| `intent at`       | Acceptance test commands                                                          | yes       | read            | --         |
| `intent at list`  | List ATs (id, reference, status)                                                  | yes       | read            | --         |
| `intent at lint`  | Check AT rows against the grammar                                                 | yes       | read            | --         |
| `intent at green` | Set an AT green                                                                   | yes       | mutate          | one-way    |
| `intent at red`   | Set an AT red                                                                     | yes       | mutate          | one-way    |
| `intent at na`    | Set a non-test AT to n/a (the doc / eyeball / gate status)                        | yes       | mutate          | one-way    |
| `intent at new`   | Create an acceptance test (caller-assigned id; refuses an id that is taken)       | yes       | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent at edit`  | Re-cite an acceptance test; a field you do not name is a field it does not change | yes       | mutate          | reversible |

## `intent at`

Acceptance test commands

```
intent at <command>
```

|                 |                                                            |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| In `v3.0.1`     | yes                                                        |
| Reads or writes | read                                                       |
| Undo            | not applicable -- the register records this verb as a read |
| Over MCP        | no                                                         |

**Arguments**

| Argument  | Type         | Required | Values | Notes |
| --------- | ------------ | -------- | ------ | ----- |
| `command` | `subcommand` | yes      |        |       |

**Exit codes** follow the surface-wide contract on the [index](index.md#exit-codes) (INV-04). `intent at --help`, and your own binary, are the authority on this verb.

## `intent at green`

```

```

Also spelled `at done`.

| --------------- | ------- |
| In `v3.0.1`     | yes     |
| Reads or writes | mutate  |
| Undo            | one-way |
| Over MCP        | yes     |

| Argument | Type    | Required | Values | Notes |
| -------- | ------- | -------- | ------ | ----- |
| `stid`   | `st-id` | yes      |        |       |
| `atid`   | `at-id` | yes      |        |       |

**Flags**

| Flag     | Takes    | Default | What it does                                                                                       |
| -------- | -------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--note` | `<text>` |         | Why the row is in this state -- carried onto the row as its note; absent, an existing note is kept |

## `intent at new`

Create an acceptance test (caller-assigned id; refuses an id that is taken)

**That description asserts a precondition, and nothing checks it.** The register has no structural home for refusals, so a refusal can only be stated as prose in a help string -- which is a contract nothing verifies and nothing updates when the behaviour moves. One of the four such strings in the surface is measured false. See issue `0142`; treat this line as a description, not a guarantee.

```
intent at new <stid> <atid> [flags]
```

|                 |            |
| --------------- | ---------- |
| In `v3.0.1`     | yes        |
| Reads or writes | mutate     |
| Undo            | reversible |
| Over MCP        | yes        |

**Arguments**

| Argument | Type    | Required | Values | Notes |
| -------- | ------- | -------- | ------ | ----- |
| `stid`   | `st-id` | yes      |        |       |
| `atid`   | `at-id` | yes      |        |       |

**Flags**

| Flag       | Takes                         | Default    | What it does                                                                                       |
| ---------- | ----------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--covers` | `<acid>...`                   |            | The criterion id(s) this test covers                                                               |
| `--file`   | `<path>`                      |            | The test file this row cites                                                                       |
| `--prose`  | `<text>`                      |            | What a non-test row asserts instead of a file                                                      |
| `--kind`   | `<test\|non-test>`            | `test`     | Test-backed or not                                                                                 |
| `--status` | `<to-write\|red\|green\|n-a>` | `to-write` | Initial status                                                                                     |
| `--note`   | `<text>`                      |            | Why the row is in this state -- carried onto the row as its note; absent, an existing note is kept |

**Exit codes** follow the surface-wide contract on the [index](index.md#exit-codes) (INV-04). `intent at new --help`, and your own binary, are the authority on this verb.

## `intent at edit`

Re-cite an acceptance test; a field you do not name is a field it does not change

```
intent at edit <stid> <atid> [flags]
```

|                 |            |
| --------------- | ---------- |
| In `v3.0.1`     | yes        |
| Reads or writes | mutate     |
| Undo            | reversible |
| Over MCP        | yes        |

**Arguments**

| Argument | Type    | Required | Values | Notes |
| -------- | ------- | -------- | ------ | ----- |
| `stid`   | `st-id` | yes      |        |       |
| `atid`   | `at-id` | yes      |        |       |

**Flags**

| Flag       | Takes              | Default | What it does                                                                                  |
| ---------- | ------------------ | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--file`   | `<path>`           |         | The repo-relative test file                                                                   |
| `--prose`  | `<text>`           |         | What was read or eyeballed (non-test rows)                                                    |
| `--kind`   | `<test\|non-test>` |         | Re-kind the row: test or non-test -- refused if the row's status cannot hold it               |
| `--covers` | `<ac-id>...`       |         | The AC id(s) this test covers, replacing the current set                                      |
| `--note`   | `<text>`           |         | Replace the row's note outright -- the deliberate door; `at green/red/na --note` only EXTENDS |

**Exit codes** follow the surface-wide contract on the [index](index.md#exit-codes) (INV-04). `intent at edit --help`, and your own binary, are the authority on this verb.

## Refusals

**There is no per-command refusal list, because the register does not carry one.** A row declares its path, arguments, flags, target, disposition, recoverability, MCP exposure and read-or-mutate, and nothing structural about what it refuses.

The estate-wide roster of refusal variants is in [what Intent ships at this revision](cut-surface.md), taken from a roster that declares itself exhaustive and is checked as one. **It is not attributed to commands anywhere**, and attributing it by reading the variant names would be a guess dressed as a reference.
